_comment: Wording of task briefs that leads agents to known mistakes when they build SA assets (satk.style.brief).
pattern = case-insensitive regular expression on the brief with line breaks joined to spaces; why = what
vanilla does instead and what went wrong; fix = what the brief should say. A brief DESCRIBES the design in
words (proportions, signature features, how the parts meet) and points to the style topics; it never sets
polygon numbers and never defines the style as numbers.

box_risk.why: box words made agents build cubes with one chamfer: a 90s SUV came out as a rectangle in plan with hard 90-degree corners, flat sides and slab flares; vanilla turns every corner in 2-3 smooth steps, crowns roof and bonnet and leans the glasshouse in
box_risk.fix: describe the shape the SA way: 'an upright body with soft, rounded corners in plan and section, crowned roof and bonnet, the glasshouse leaning in'

style_numbers.pattern: \b(san andreas\s+)?style\W{0,3}\s+(means|is|=)\s+(the\s+)?(measured|numbers|bands|data|metrics)\b|\bmeasured (bands|data, not adjectives)\b|\bnot adjectives\b|\bin numbers\b|\b(inside|within) the (class |tier |sa_plus |vanilla )?bands?\b|\bclass bands? (decide|decides)\b|\bout-of-band\b|\bevery metric\b
style_numbers.why: 'style = numbers' made agents chase bands: one dissolved coplanar faces to move shade and dihedral numbers into band (no pixel changed) and capped the car's length at a class percentile; the SA look is a description (soft, rounded, simplified forms; small soft photo textures), vanilla numbers are reference only
style_numbers.fix: describe the look and cite the style topics; say 'vanilla numbers are reference, never targets'

tri_numbers.why: triangle numbers turn style into counting: a 4,500 cap made an agent re-box a rounded bumper (bevel segments 2 -> 1) and a band floor kept another from adding detail; counts are a result, never a target
tri_numbers.fix: describe the detail wanted (interior, engine bay, lamp housings) and let the forms take what they need

low_poly.why: 'low-poly' reads as faceted boxes; vanilla is soft and rounded, with density only where the outline turns
low_poly.fix: say 'soft, rounded, simplified surfaces; detail where it reads at game distance'

measure_photo.why: measuring pixels of a three-quarter photo (grids, solved cameras, back-projection) gave wrong local proportions; SA keeps the silhouette lines, simplifies and widens
measure_photo.fix: describe the references (a features list per photo); measure only true side, front or rear views

dirty.why: painted grime made a car look filthy at every dirt level; vanilla paint is a clean key colour times vehiclegrunge256 and the engine adds the dirt
dirty.fix: say 'small, soft, photo-like textures with light and folds painted in; car paint a clean key colour'

detail_texture.pattern: \bdetail (is|belongs) (in(to)? )?(the )?texture,? not (in )?(the )?geometry\b|\b(are|is) texture or flush details?, not geometry\b
detail_texture.why: 'detail is texture, not geometry' left vehicles without lamp housings, grille surrounds and interiors; richer modelled detail in the same soft style is welcome
detail_texture.fix: say 'model what reads at game distance (lamps in recesses, grille surround, mirrors, handles, interior, engine bay); paint what is fine or flat'

crisp.why: vanilla textures are small, soft and photo-like (hundreds of colours, soft light); 'crisp' produces vector-art textures with a few flat colours
crisp.fix: say 'small, soft, photo-like textures with light and folds painted in' and cite style_texture

clean_shapes.why: 'clean shapes' gave bare, under-detailed models made of plain primitives; vanilla bodies are soft and rounded and carry lamps, trim, mirrors and handles
clean_shapes.fix: describe the forms ('soft, rounded, simplified forms joined into one body') and the details that must be modelled

flat_colour.why: vanilla paint is the key colour times vehiclegrunge256 (grain, dirt, height-dependent value) plus the env sheen; map materials are textured and prelit
flat_colour.fix: say 'paint on vehiclegrunge256 with the class colour keys' (vehicles) or 'tiling textures with prelight' (map)

no_photos.why: vanilla textures are photo-sourced; a ban on photographs pushes agents to vector art
no_photos.fix: allow licensed photographs or name the photo-like recipe of style_texture

real_scale.why: SA vehicles are about 1.1-1.2x their real counterparts and relatively wider, with real-size wheels; real-world specs made the benchmark car 4.98 m, below every vanilla 4-door
real_scale.fix: say 'scale from the anchor (the wheel of the class or the ped height); keep the real car's ratios, a little larger and wider'

hard_edges.why: vanilla cars are soft (normal bend about 10 deg); 80-93 % of their hard edges sit on material or UV seams and 22-45 % of their 60-90 deg folds stay smooth
hard_edges.fix: say 'smooth inside a material, split normals at seams and designed creases' and cite style_shading

dam_lighter.pattern: _dam\b[^.]{0,60}\b(not more than|no more than|never (more|heavier)( than)?|fewer (triangles )?than|lighter than|less than)\b
dam_lighter.why: vanilla _dam parts are dented copies of their _ok part; a 'never heavier' rule makes agents decimate the damage states
dam_lighter.fix: say 'damage parts built from the _ok parts (kit.damage), visibly dented'

from_nothing.why: rebuilding from scripts made agents hand-type thousands of coordinates; reproducibility comes from the session journal and checkpoints
from_nothing.fix: say 'model in the live Blender session; asset.json, the journal and checkpoints make it reproducible'
